10. Mr. Fazlul Haque the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant petitioners has taken us through the judgment of the courts below and evidence, both oral documentary as marked exhibits by the Trial Court and submitted that the learned Assistant Judge on proper discussions of the oral and documentary evidence decided the issue 'No.4 that the plaintiffs is not in possession of the suit property and that the deed- of gifts made in favour of the deities in the year 1333 and 1351 B.S. were acted upon, but the Appellate Court without properly adverted to the evidence has reserved those findings and that judgment being not a proper judgment of reversal has committed error of law which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He further contended that issue No.6 and 7 were decided against the plaintiffs and that the Appellate Court has not reversed the findings of the Trial Court to the effect that the plaintiff had failed to produce any witness to prove the name of any creditor of late Ramani Mohan before the Court nor any name of any creditor was mentioned in the plaint to prove that the deed of gift in faour of the deities were executed and registered by Ramani to defraud the creditor and arrived at an erroneous findings which has resulted an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The Appellate Court has utterly failed to consider that Rash Behari Das became a Baishnab and not only be changed his name as Ramani Das Baishnab but also changed his life style and in doing so he and dedicated his property in the name of the deities and his homestead was turned into Akhra Bari which are being transpired from exhibit "Go Series" and that the Appellate Court also failed to notice that some of the properties were recorded in the name of the deities and some of the lands of Raekhail Mouja were recorded in the name of Ramani for which Ramani filed an application before the A.D.0 (Revenue), Sylhet for correction of record of rights in the name of the deities, which has been marked as exhibit-Cha and his intention thereby, was proved that he dedicated his whole life for religious purpose but the teamed Appellate Court arrived at an erroneous decision in setting aside the judgment of the Trial Court which has clearly caused failure of justice. The Appellate Court on the face of the record has erred in recording his self contradictory and misconceived findings while considering the evidence of PW.2 regarding Akhra Bah and also made findings as to Braja Bala Baishnabi without considering the evidence to its true perspective but arrived at an erroneous findings and decision and thus acted upon erroneous view which has occasioned failure of justice. He further contended that the Appellate Court has grossly misread the evidence of PW.2 and DW.1 in as much as the deities are now in the custody of the Shebait DW.1 in his own house and the homestead of Ramoni which is the Akhrabari has vacant house. Sheba-Puja of the deities has been performing by the committed approved by the learned District Judge but such fact and evidence were not correctly appreciated and came to the wrong finding which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He submitted further that the Appellate Court has come to wrong findings that Ramoni Mohan Das Baishnab during his life time realized rents from the tenants and also filed rent suits in his own name and from the exhibit 9(ka), 10-10(ka), it disclosed Ramoni himself did not implement the deed of gift in favour of deities are misconceived findings and those were not in issue before the court and recording finding beyond the scope of the suit has committed error of law which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 17. In view of the aforesaid judgments, the prime question before us, whether the deeds admittedly executed by the Rash Behari Das alias Ramoni Mohan Das were acted upon. In view of judgment of reversal, I have very meticulously gone through the judgment of both the courts and also the oral and documentary evidence to arrive at my own findings. It appears, the Trial Court has interpreted the evidence in the light of the order passed in Miscellaneous Case No.59 of 1972, exhibits Cha, Chaa and Chaa(1) the resolution book.
